route_definitions.computer_use: Operate a live desktop, browser, or mobile GUI via screenshots, mouse clicks, keyboard input, or window automation.
route_definitions.visual_analysis: Inspect, compare, or classify static images, photos, screenshots, UI mockups, or design frames (from coarse OCR to layout diffs and fine-grained styling/material/lighting judgment) without operating a live GUI or editing UI code.
route_definitions.frontend_implementation: Implement, style, or fix UI components, layouts, CSS, React/Vue/Tkinter views, charts, or visual interactions in code.
route_definitions.general_implementation: Implement, modify, or refactor backend, CLI, service, automation, or library code in a repository.
route_definitions.debug_review: Diagnose a bug, race, crash, or latency regression; fix an isolated defect; OR perform a read-only code/diff/branch/security/release audit.
route_definitions.exploration_analysis: Read-only codebase exploration, dependency mapping, log/telemetry forensics, or architectural tracing.
route_definitions.research_packet: Execute a quantitative experiment, backtest, statistical evaluation, or benchmark packet on local data and report metrics.
route_definitions.web_research: Survey public documentation, vendor specs, open-web articles, cultural motifs, or literature and synthesize findings (even if saving output to a local path).
route_definitions.text_in_text_out: Draft, translate, polish, or restructure self-contained text, narrative dialogue, or documentation when required source material is already inlined.
route_definitions.self_contained_code: Write or verify a standalone algorithm, data structure, or script whose specification and inputs are self-contained in the brief without reading local repo modules.
route_definitions.bounded_bulk_work: Apply a uniform mechanical edit/checklist across many files, OR traverse many local files to extract one structured record per item into an inventory/table.
route_definitions.tool_execution: Run an explicit operational runbook, build/release/git pipeline, CLI sequence, or non-GUI API observe-act loop.
route_definitions.complex_build_plan: Author a multi-phase engineering specification, system migration plan, or whole-system architectural blueprint before implementation.
route_definitions.direction_reasoning: High-depth mathematical proof/derivation, formal critique, or first-principles system/mechanism design.

dimension_rubric.anti_inflation_rule: Score ONLY functional work the worker performs, never brief length or Markdown structure. Coordinator headers (`Parent session agent ID`, `工作目录`), role/AGENTS/SKILL docs, communication contracts, and output/receipt paths are boilerplate—ignore them for `reasoning_depth`, `code_complexity`, and `axis_demand`.
dimension_rubric.local_only_positive_vs_negative: CONTRAST RULE for `local_only`: `true` when depending on un-inlined files/dirs/repos on THIS machine (reading, copying, searching, editing, building, or testing local files) or local processes/daemons/GUI/env. `false` when all required inputs are inlined or from the public web (`web_research`, `self_contained_code`, `text_in_text_out`, `direction_reasoning`, `complex_build_plan`), even if a workspace header or local output path is named.
dimension_rubric.visual_vs_live_loop: CONTRAST RULE for `needs_visual`, `needs_gui`, `aesthetics`, and `tool_operation`: (1) Static offline image/photo/screenshot inspection (`visual_analysis`) sets `needs_visual: true, needs_gui: false`, scores visual difficulty on `aesthetics` (`1` coarse OCR/text extraction, `2` UI layout/spacing/typography diff, `3` fine-grained styling/garment/makeup/material/lighting/color-cast perception), and keeps `tool_operation` at `0..1`. (2) Operating a live GUI or watching a continuously changing screen (`computer_use`) sets `needs_visual: true, needs_gui: true, tool_operation: 3`. (3) Non-GUI live API/CLI observe-act loops set `needs_visual: false, needs_gui: false, tool_operation: 2`. (4) Writing, fixing, or analyzing logs of real-time/game/ticket/trading software is `coding` / `exploration_analysis` (`tool_operation: 0..1`), NOT a live loop.
dimension_rubric.read_only_review: CONTRAST RULE for `read_only_review` & `access`: `read_only_review: true` ONLY for read-only code/PR/diff/branch/security/release audits that modify NO repo code (`code_complexity: 0, access: "read-only", work_kind: "debug_review"`, even if saving a review report file). `false` for runtime/log diagnosis without a diff audit (`access: "read-only"`), ops runbooks, or fixing findings from a prior review (`access: "write", code_complexity > 0`).
dimension_rubric.wants_fast: CONTRAST RULE for `wants_fast`: `true` ONLY when affirmatively requesting fast mode, priority tier, urgent/ASAP turnaround, or a pre-reset quota sprint (`pre-reset sprint`, `before quota resets`, `重置前冲刺`) without negation. `false` when negated (`Do NOT use fast mode`, `no rush`, `不用开启fast`), when fast/immediate only describes an in-task step (`click Save immediately`), when merely mentioning quota/reset in code/tests, or when unmentioned.
dimension_rubric.reasoning_depth: `1` (Routine): explicit command/checklist/runbook, trivial config tweak, one-off GUI click, or mechanical bulk edit; `2` (Standard/Hard): single/multi-module feature, bug diagnosis/fix, read-only PR/visual audit, research packet, or structured synthesis; `3` (Coupled): cross-module refactor with strict invariants, multi-hypothesis concurrency/leak forensics, or subsystem migration; `4` (Frontier): whole-system architecture from scratch, game/economy/network mathematical mechanism design, or formal proof/critique.
dimension_rubric.multi_task_vs_single_task: `multi_task: true` ONLY when bundling 2+ independent deliverables assignable to separate workers in parallel. Sequential steps (`diagnose -> fix -> test -> report`) or one batch/report covering multiple items is ONE task (`multi_task: false, task_count: "1"`).
dimension_rubric.axis_demand: Level 0..3 per category: divergence: 0 execute an explicit spec, runbook, or mechanical checklist, 1 routine engineering or inspection with small local judgment calls or wording choices, 2 generate and compare multiple options or hypotheses, or investigate and synthesize a research, log, or data-analysis question, 3 open-ended creative writing, broad synthesis across many sources, or first-principles architecture/system design from scratch. coding: 0 no source code read, reviewed, or written, 1 a small helper script, config/constant tweak, log-analysis snippet, or running an existing test/CLI check, 2 implement, fix, refactor, or review/audit a production module with its tests, 3 coupled multi-module architecture, concurrency/lock/protocol invariants, whole-system code audit, or high-blast-radius irreversible changes. aesthetics: 0 no visual output and no image or screenshot inspection, 1 plain text, tables, or structured reports where only clean formatting matters, or coarse OCR/text extraction from a simple screenshot, 2 implement or style a user-facing UI, page, or chart whose look matters, or compare/audit screenshots and mockups for layout, spacing, typography, and component state, 3 design-led visual creation (new interface/interaction system, visual identity, 2D/3D scene) OR fine-grained visual perception and aesthetic classification (judging outfit/garment/makeup styling, material/texture, lighting, color cast, or subtle visual artifacts across images). tool_operation: 0 self-contained reasoning/writing, or reading/editing local files and running a few shell/test commands, 1 routine CLI, git, web-search, API, or batch local file/image inspection calls without real-time latency pressure, 2 heavy multi-step tool/API orchestration, or the worker itself stays in a live text/API observe-act loop (live order book, ticket API polling, live chat stream) where slow turns degrade the outcome, 3 operate a desktop, browser, or mobile GUI via screenshots/clicks/keys, or continuously watch and react to a live changing visual screen inside a real-time loop.
dimension_rubric.expected_hours: Measured agent pace: quick check, runbook, single-diff review, or screenshot check = 0.1-0.25h; standard investigation, bug fix, batch visual audit, or 1-5 file feature with tests = 0.3-0.6h; wide 8+ file refactor or broad web survey = 0.8-2.5h; multi-stage build or sustained multi-hour live loop = 2.5-4h+. Brief length and boilerplate add nothing.

# Task: Implement standalone weighted interval merger (`tools/interval_merger.py`)

## Specification (Self-Contained)
Write a pure Python 3.11 module `interval_merger.py` with no third-party dependencies that implements:
`merge_weighted_intervals(intervals: list[tuple[int, int, float]], min_gap: int = 0) -> list[tuple[int, int, float]]`
Rules:
- Intervals are half-open `[start, end)` with `start < end` and positive float weight.
- Overlapping or adjacent intervals within `min_gap` merge into `[min_start, max_end)` with length-weighted average weight.
- Include a `unittest` suite covering empty input, nested intervals, negative coordinates, and `min_gap > 0`.
